takeaways: Fretless banjo lets you slide into notes for an older, modal sound
'The Cuckoo' is a standard every old-time player learns

title: Cookie-tin fretless banjo — a DIY instrument built with a parent

takeaways: A cookie tin works as a banjo resonator for a cheap DIY build
Fretless necks are simpler to build and suit old-time modal tunes
Building an instrument with family is a good maker project

title: Ievan Polkka in Russian — the Finnish polka with new lyrics

takeaways: The scat chorus survives translation intact; that's the hook
Folk narratives (forbidden dance) adapt easily across cultures

takeaways: Triple-repeated phrases ('Irish eyes, Irish eyes') make an instant earworm
Parent-inheritance imagery is a strong lyrical frame

title: 'Shady Grove' — from Renaissance ballad to Appalachian standard

title: The khaen — Lao bamboo free-reed organ that plays on inhale and exhale
summary: Explainer on the khaen from Laos and Isan: bamboo pipes with metal free reeds, played by both blowing and drawing breath like a harmonica, so it can sustain continuous sound and simple chords. Its buzzing, hypnotic tone now shows up in electronic and ambient music.
techniques: circular sound via blow and draw
takeaways: Free reeds sound on both inhale and exhale, enabling continuous drones
Can play chords, so it works as a pad source in ambient production
Same instrument family as harmonica and sheng
